name: Measured Joules, Learned Routes: Learning to Route for Energy-Efficient LLM Serving
problem: Most queries do not need the largest model, and routing them to a high-capability model burns unnecessary compute AND energy — but energy is not what existing quality routers optimise.
mechanism: Profile every candidate model per query in an OFFLINE TOURNAMENT recording correctness, latency, power and GPU energy; then train an LM-based router by supervised fine-tuning followed by group relative policy optimization (GRPO) on those measurements, so routing is optimised against the accuracy-ENERGY tradeoff rather than accuracy alone.
speedup_reported: Per the arXiv abstract, learned routing improves the accuracy-energy tradeoff in multi-LLM serving across several candidate pools; the abstract's quantitative claim is truncated and no single multiple with baseline and settings is stated, so no bare number is recorded. The mechanism is the contribution: energies are MEASURED per candidate per query in an offline tournament, which is the only way an online router can know joules rather than guess them from model size.
notes:
Venue arxiv-preprint, and the arXiv comment says 'in submission' — explicitly NOT accepted anywhere as of this record. Recorded here as the energy-aware counterpart to RouteLLM: same routing shape, different objective function, and the objective is the actual novelty. Read alongside the PRISM record — if PRISM is right that carbon is not proportional to joules, then optimising joules is a first-order improvement over optimising nothing but an incomplete answer.
